finding_key: packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts::bulk yorkie maintenance scripts now rewrite every document's last-modified time and scramble the global list ordering
evidence: The mechanism is real: `migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts` (`migrateDocument` → `doc.update(replaceYorkieRoot)` + `client.sync`) and `migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts` both perform root-content mutations on `sheet-<id>` docs, and `yorkie-event.controller.ts` unconditionally calls `documentService.touchUpdatedAt(parsed.id, min(issuedAt, now))` for any `DocumentRootChanged` without distinguishing maintenance writes from user edits — so a bulk migration run after the webhook is registered would bump `updatedAt` for every changed doc and show a false "Last modified" in the list ordered by `[{updatedAt:desc},{createdAt:desc}]` (document.controller.ts). Two mitigations the prose ignores: both scripts iterate `orderBy: createdAt asc`, so the resulting order is ≈`createdAt desc` (the pre-PR default) rather than a scramble, and `copy-yorkie-documents.ts` writes to a separate target cluster where this project's webhook isn't registered. It also requires a condition not yet true in the merged state (webhook registration is still an unchecked post-merge ops item) plus a future run of a one-shot migration script, so I score this as a genuine but minor blast-radius/data-fidelity side effect rather than a functional defect.
